entities.title: A Durable Object per online game, the game in D1
entities.summary: Each online game's actions pass through its own GameRoom, one at a time; the game itself is stored in D1.
entities.context: Two players act on the same game at once and both must see every change; lists and history must query games.
entities.decision: GameRoom, named by the game's id, queues actions (RoomCore), saves to D1 only if the game is unchanged, and broadcasts to hibernatable WebSockets. The lobby, history and contacts query D1 directly.
entities.rationale: Two moves can never race, an idle game costs nothing while its sockets hibernate, and D1 can list games by player.

entities.title: icelander.net's one sign-in instead of Gambit's own
entities.summary: Gambit no longer signs people in itself: icelander.net's login service does, for every game under icelander.net/games.
entities.context: Gambit had its own Google and GitHub OAuth, a chess_session cookie and a sessions table; the games are part of icelander.net and share one sign-in.
entities.decision: Check the host's site_session through vendor/icelander-auth and the ACCOUNTS binding; keep Gambit's users table keyed by address, so a person plays as the first of their addresses Gambit already knows; send the old login and callback addresses to the host's sign-in.
entities.rationale: One sign-in for the whole host; players keep their games, contacts and history.

relationships.description: The GDD's decision that multiplayer uses Gambit's own OAuth sign-in.

entities.title: Should the API require the games:play role?
entities.summary: The page needs a sign-in with games:play; the API needs only a sign-in.
entities.context: index.ts serves the page through requirePlayer (AUTH.requireRole with games:play), but handleApi uses currentUser, which accepts anyone the login service knows, with or without the role. Rally's Worker checks the role on its API too.

options.title: Require games:play on the API as on the page
options.consequences: A person without the role can do nothing through the API either; /api/me would have to keep answering signed-out and role-less callers in a way the client understands.

options.title: Keep the API open to anyone signed in
options.consequences: Someone signed in to icelander.net without games:play can invite, play and keep history by calling the API directly.
